expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Could have had a much bigger day last week if not for some drops by his WRs. This is another defense that has struggled in the secondary, and this game has all the makings of a track meet.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Lions are allowing over 300 yards passing a game, and the Packers have been ascending over the last few weeks.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Hard to pass on Jordan Love this week, especially in cash games, as he is playing some of the best football of his career. On top of that, he gets back a playmaker in Josh Jacobs and faces a Lions secondary that has struggled to stop opposing QBs. The Lions allow the most fantasy points to opposing QBs and the 4th most EPA/Pass.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Stacking against the Lions workd, so let's stick with it. Josh Jacobs should be back for Green Bay, but I still expect a below-average rushing attack. Love is having a career year because the Packers can’t stop anyone and have had to throw more. His aDOT (9.1) and XFPPG (20.1) are among the best on the slate. Detroit is 30th in EPA allowed per dropback and last in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to QBs.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: The Lions have absolutely been torched by opposing offenses and Love has three elite targets in Christian Watson, Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden, not to mention getting Josh Jacobs back this week.  This is one of the best possible matchups for Love and he has been performing better and better each week!

players.notes: Faces a vulnerable secondary in a high-total matchup with weapons returning.
Strong passing volume in a high-total home game against Atlanta.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Young doesn’t stand out in most projections, so ownership should stay low. He has been even better than he was late last year, with a +5.6% CPOE and regular shots downfield. Carolina is 1st in neutral pace and 3rd in explosive play rate, and Young is averaging 22 fantasy points a game with almost nothing from his legs. Tampa Bay has one of the league’s best run defenses, so the Panthers should lean on the pass.

players.notes: Leans heavily on pass volume with a Strong neutral pace and deep shots.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Stroud is playing as well as just about any QB this season, and this week he'll have not only Nico Collins and his favorite college WR, but also Tank Dell back in the mix, a receiver he's already shown great chemistry with in the NFL.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Stroud has really turned it around from last season and now has a plethora of weapons at WR with the expected return of Tank Dell and newly acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. The Texans have one of the highest implied team totals on the slate and faces a Giants team that has allowed some solid QB scores on the season. Would limit Stroud to GPPs-only.

players.notes: Boosted pass volume with returning weapons against a weak Giants defense.
High pass volume in a favorable game environment with a 53.5 total.
Solid home underdog spot with a decent 43.5 game total.
Reliable passing floor in a tight divisional matchup.
Solid home favorite spot with a high 48.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: It is hard to ignore Gibbs most weeks in cash, but this week Gibbs gets a matchup with the Packers team that has struggled to keep RBs out of the endzone (allowing 1.5 RB TDs per game). Opposing running backs have accounted for approximately 40% of fantasy points allowed by the Packers this season, 3rd most in the NFL. Lions also have the highest team total on the slate and Gibbs is a perfect runback to Jordan Love. Play with confidence in all formats.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: I love this entire game and will have plenty of Packers, but Gibbs will be my highest-owned bring back option on the Detroit side.  He gets the Packers defense, who have given up big numbers to RB's and they recently let Bijan Robinson have a huge game and I expect Gibbs to put up similar numbers.

players.notes: Elite touch volume in a great matchup against a leaky run defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I’ll match the field on Jahmyr Gibbs and go overweight on McCaffrey, who is too cheap, especially on DraftKings. With Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel out, even more of the offense runs through him. His snap share is up to 72%, he has the goal-line work to himself, and he runs a route on 20% of dropbacks. I wouldn’t be surprised by 10+ targets. Atlanta is 30th in EPA against the run and 23rd in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

players.notes: Increased snap share and goal-line work with key pass-catchers sidelined.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Brian Robinson is out, which should lead to as much work for Bijan as possible in this one. The 49ers concede a significant amount of receiving work to opposing RBs, and Nick Bosa did not practice on Friday.

players.notes: Heavy touch volume and Strong receiving role against a depleted front.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Marks has firmly established himself as the Texans' RB1 over the last two games, and I think this is a matchup where he can put up a massive performance. The Giants have struggled against the run, but they've also had issues defending RBs out of the backfield. That gives Marks multiple ways to take advantage of this defense, and I expect Houston to lean on him both as a runner and in the passing game.

players.notes: Firmly established as the lead runner with heavy involvement in the passing.
Strong workload as the primary option for a favored home offense.
Feature role in the run game against a struggling Minnesota front.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Over their last three games, the Bengals have allowed the third-most rushing yards before contact in the NFL. Derrick Henry is one of the most dangerous RBs we've ever seen when he gets past the line of scrimmage without being touched, and Cincinnati's inability to stop runners before they get into the second level makes this a fantastic matchup for him.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Ravens OL should get a boost with the expected debut of Cam Jurgens at Center, allowing Olaivavega Ioane to slide back to his natural position at guard. Henry has averaged 23.2 touches per game, with at least 18 in all games and has also contributed with 8 TDs on the season. The Bengals have been playing with light boxes on a league-high 40% of run plays which is something Henry rarely gets to see (sub 10% of the time). The Bengals rush defense is also bottom 10 in YPC, 10-plus yard runs, yards before contact, and yards after contact. All signs that point to the King dominating.

players.notes: Heavy rushing volume against a defense struggling with contact yards.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Running back is an incredibly tricky position this week. You either spend top dollar on the absolute stars or you're left with very few desirable options after that. Pollard has a great price on both sites, a winnable matchup, and very little competition among DFS running backs in his price range.

players.notes: Affordable salary and clear backfield role in a low-total matchup.
Solid rushing share in a competitive divisional game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Wouldn't fault you to play Golden or Watson in this matchup (or even both). However, Golden comes at a discount on both sites which makes him the easy plug and play. Golden now has a 100+ yard game in 3 of his last 4, as well as a TD in 3 of his last 4 (should have had a multi-TD game vs Dallas). Golden and Watson both have WR1 numbers and both have amazing matchups vs this bleak Lions secondary. Lions have opted to play more single-high zone coverage over the last few weeks and Golden currently leads the team in target rate and yards per route run vs those looks. On the year, Golden is top 12 in target share, top 10 in air yards, and top 3 in redzone targets.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Regular readers know I’m a fan of Golden. His underlying usage has been better than Christian Watson’s all season, yet his salary keeps coming in lower, and that’s true again this week after a 6-104-1 game. The Packers should stay pass-heavy, especially if they fall behind early against a Lions defense that is 30th in EPA allowed per dropback and 31st in fantasy points allowed to WRs. I’ll have some Watson too, but I like Golden more.

players.notes: Leads the team in target rate against single-high zone coverages.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: If there was ever a week for a Waddle breakout, it would be this one. Cardinals allow the 3rd highest EPA/pass and is the clear #1 (leads team in targets and yards). Cardinals have been torched by WR1s; allowing the 3rd most fantasy points to opposing #1s, 2nd most yards per target and league-high TD rate. If there was ever a game for Waddle to show why Denver acquired him, this would be the game. Waddle exclusive to GPP-only formats.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: The peripheral metrics for Jaylen Waddle are in lne with his career averages. The Cardinals are a bottom-3 pass defense and there is no chance that Bo Nix can play this bad for this long.

players.notes: Clear role as the primary target facing a bottom-three pass defense.
Strong route participation and consistent targets in Carolina's offense.
Consistent target share in a fast-paced game with a high total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: London's price tag is so much more appealing on FanDuel relative to the salary cap. The 49ers defense has put up some good numbers this year, but they've actually only faced a couple of top WRs. Games against Miami, Arizona, Denver (which doesn't even attempt downfield passes), and Washington (where McLaurin was injured early) have skewed those numbers, in my opinion.

players.notes: Strong target volume with a favorable Price on FanDuel.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Nuclear ceiling pivot from the chalkier WRs, especially in the Packers/Lions game, especially now with Puka banged up.

players.notes: Elite target share in a competitive divisional matchup.
Solid downfield role and route participation in an up-tempo offense.
Elite target volume as the focal point of the Minnesota passing attack.
High target share and deep route participation as the primary weapon.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: There isn't anybody else left to throw the ball to for the 49ers, and the Falcons haven't defended TEs well in the red-zone. Waller had two touchdowns, and Loveland should've had two as well.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: The Niners are down their top two receivers, Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans, so George Kittle is essentially their WR1 while still being listed, and priced, as a tight end. He already had a 21% target share and a 22% air yards share with those two on the field. This one doesn’t need much thought, especially since the Falcons have been a bottom-10 defense against tight ends.

players.notes: Acts as the primary pass-catcher with key wide receivers sidelined.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Tucker Kraft is playable in all formats. We have targeted TEs vs Lions all year, and we will continue here. Kraft should be a fraction of the ownership of his teammates in Golden and Watson and has just as good of a matchup. While the return of Brian Branch should help the Lions' TE struggles, I still think this is more of duct tape on a leaky faucet type of fix. Kraft TD will be a prop I really like this week.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Lions have been the worst team in the NFL against TEs to this point in the season, which is saying something given how bad the Commanders are. We know Kraft has a monster ceiling from what he showed last season, and his route participation is up in the 70+% range after a lesser role in week one. He makes for an awesome pivot off his very chalky WR teammates, and a couple other very popular TEs.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Tucker Kraft has a great price on both sites and he gets the perfect matchup against the Lions, who continue to give up big points to opposing TE's.  Kraft has been getting between 5-8 targets the last 5 games and he is a huge red zone target for Jordan Love.  This could be a breakout game for Kraft and I have been playing him since the start of the season and won't stop now.

players.notes: High route participation against a defense struggling heavily against tight.
High value salary option with consistent route volume.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Likely is another elite TE target this week along with Tucker Kraft and I don't mind lineups where you land on both.  They both have high ceilings and Likely is getting lots of looks and red zone targets in the Giants offense.

players.notes: Frequent red-zone looks and Strong route volume in the passing game.
Strong route rate and red-zone usage in a high-total matchup.
Elite target volume and seam usage in a high-total game.
Red-zone target upside in a fast-paced divisional matchup.
Elite route rate and reliable seam usage against a vulnerable secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: The Higbee/Ferguson role is vital to the Rams offense without Davante Adams. If Puka doens't pay, the floor for Higbee goes even higher but I do think the overall offensive volume for the Rams diminishes.

players.notes: Vital role in the passing game with expanded snaps available.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: A cheap defense against Deshaun Watson; simple play.
